chapter_02_finding: 3 exact duplicate rows found (rows 301-303, copies of 16, 88, 151).
evidence_reviewed: patient_id duplication check; rows 301-303 are exact duplicates across all columns.
rationale: Exact duplicates inflate sample size artificially and bias parameters.
analytical_consequence: Correct sample size for unbiased estimations.

chapter_02_finding: Age of -5 years found for patient 32.
action_taken: Recoded age = -5 to NA and imputed using median age (53).
analytical_consequence: Maintains sample size; age parameter estimates are unbiased by impossible values.

chapter_02_finding: Age of 115 years found for patients 47, 93, 236.
evidence_reviewed: Centenarian patient literature and clinical database records.
action_taken: Retained age = 115 unchanged, documented for sensitivity analysis.
rationale: High age is biologically possible and represents valid extreme clinical observations.
analytical_consequence: High-leverage points can be tested for sensitivity.

chapter_02_finding: Systolic BP of 280 mmHg found for patients 181, 209, 268.
evidence_reviewed: Near-normal diastolic readings (68, 71, 93 mmHg) and lack of hypertension diagnosis; clinical implausibility.
action_taken: Recoded systolic_bp = 280 to NA and imputed using median systolic BP (121 mmHg after rounding).
rationale: 280 mmHg with normal diastolic values represents key-entry errors rather than true clinical crisis.
analytical_consequence: Prevents distortion of systolic BP regression coefficients and linear assumptions.

chapter_02_finding: A1C of 1.5% found for patients 99, 172, 251 (two are diabetic).
evidence_reviewed: Biochemically invalid level for living humans; diabetes diagnosis mismatch.
action_taken: Recoded a1c = 1.5 to NA and imputed along with missing A1Cs using median A1C (5.8%).
rationale: A1C < 3.0% is biochemically impossible for a living human.
analytical_consequence: A1C clinical significance is preserved in predictive models.

chapter_02_finding: Wait days of -3 found for patients 31, 112, 117, 132.
evidence_reviewed: Booking date recorded as after visit date.
rationale: Wait days cannot be negative; 0 assumes walk-in/same-day booking.
analytical_consequence: Lag time modeling is chronologically valid.

chapter_02_finding: Casing mismatch: 5 rows contain lowercase 'medicaid' instead of 'Medicaid'.
evidence_reviewed: Insurance value counts showing Medicaid and medicaid categories.
action_taken: Consolidated lowercase 'medicaid' to Title Case 'Medicaid' and trimmed whitespace.
rationale: Inconsistent casing splits one logical category, introducing redundant parameters.
analytical_consequence: Category counts match data dictionary, reducing model parameters.

chapter_02_finding: Value mismatch: 5 rows contain abbreviation 'y' instead of 'Yes'.
evidence_reviewed: Transportation access counts showing No, Yes, y categories.
action_taken: Consolidated 'y' abbreviation to 'Yes' and trimmed whitespace.
rationale: Abbreviation splits positive response class, reducing group statistical power.
analytical_consequence: Consolidates group power for statistical testing.

chapter_02_finding: 8 blank string values representing missing clinic locations.
evidence_reviewed: Clinic location value count showing 8 blank string values.
rationale: Allows retention of observations in modeling without complete-case deletion.

chapter_02_finding: 8 blank string values representing missing visit reasons.
evidence_reviewed: Visit reason value count showing 8 blank string values.
rationale: Allows retention of observations in modeling without complete-case deletion.

chapter_02_finding: 8 NA values in Body Mass Index.
action_taken: Imputed 8 missing values using median BMI (29.1).
rationale: Preserves statistical power and avoids selection bias in multivariable regression.
analytical_consequence: Maintains statistical power of multivariable clinical models.

chapter_02_finding: 7 NA values in A1C blood measure.
action_taken: Imputed 10 missing values (7 raw NAs + 3 recoded NAs) using median A1C (5.8%).
rationale: Preserves statistical power and avoids selection bias in multivariable regression.
analytical_consequence: Maintains statistical power of multivariable clinical models.

chapter_02_finding: Severe class imbalance in RAW data (before deduplication, N = 303): 30 missed appointments (9.9%) vs 273 completed (90.1%); cleaned sample (N = 300) has 270 completed (90.0%) and 30 missed (10.0%).
action_taken: Retained original values unchanged. Flagged class imbalance constraints.
rationale: Altering outcome variables to balance classes would distort real-world population parameters.
before_condition: RAW (before deduplication, N = 303): 273 completed (90.1%) vs 30 missed (9.9%)
after_condition: Cleaned (after deduplication, N = 300): 270 completed (90.0%) vs 30 missed (10.0%)
analytical_consequence: Limits multivariable predictor degrees of freedom in modeling to 2-3.

chapter_02_finding: Rare outcome: only 1 'Yes' case out of 303 rows.
action_taken: Retained original values unchanged. Flagged model convergence limits.
rationale: Altering rare outcomes to balance classes would distort real-world clinical rates.
analytical_consequence: Regression models will fail; must analyze emergency referrals descriptively only.

chapter_02_finding: 6 post-outcome variables (satisfaction, costs, health improvement, followup) included in raw predictors.
evidence_reviewed: Measurement timing framework mapping variables from T0 to T4.
action_taken: Retained original variables. Flagged post-visit outcomes for modeling exclusion.
rationale: Using post-visit outcomes to predict attendance causes temporal data leakage, rendering models invalid.
before_condition: 6 post-outcome variables treated as general features
after_condition: 6 post-outcome variables retained but flagged as leakage predictors
analytical_consequence: Prevents outcome-derived and temporal leakage in predictive modeling.
